title: Changer la place pour préciser le sens
summary: Choose adjective position for former versus old, own versus clean and other common meaning contrasts.
objectives: Use six frequent adjective-position contrasts in clear contexts.
Avoid treating figurative-before/literal-after as a universal rule.

sources.label: University of Texas: adjective placement and meaning
B1 public topic index (coverage reference only)

sections.title: Former or old; own or clean
paragraphs: `Ancien` before a role or relationship commonly means former: `une ancienne collègue` is someone who used to be a colleague, not necessarily an elderly person. After an object noun, `ancien` often means old or antique. Context and fixed combinations still matter; position is a useful contrast, not a machine that assigns one meaning to every noun.

`Propre` before a noun, usually after a possessive, emphasizes ownership: `sa propre voiture`, her own car. After a noun or after `être`, `propre` commonly means clean. It can also occur in other constructions such as `propre à`, suitable for or characteristic of, which are not the own/clean contrast.
points: Vocabulary: `un collègue / une collègue` (masculine/feminine), a colleague; `une armoire` (feminine), a wardrobe; `un outil` (masculine), a tool.

examples.french: Mon **ancienne** responsable dirige maintenant une école.
examples.english: My former manager now runs a school.
examples.note: She no longer holds the earlier role.

examples.english: We are restoring an antique wardrobe.

examples.note: This describes their condition, not ownership.

mistakes.avoid: Mon collègue ancien a changé d'entreprise.
mistakes.prefer: Mon ancien collègue a changé d'entreprise.
mistakes.why: To say former colleague, put `ancien` before the role noun; the original is not the ordinary way to express that meaning.

sections.title: A particular one or a sure one; dear or expensive
paragraphs: Before a noun, `certain` can mean a particular but not fully identified person or thing: `une certaine adresse`. In the plural, `certains/certaines` before a noun means some. After a noun or after `être`, `certain` means definite or sure: `un résultat certain`; `elle est certaine`. It does not mean a specific selected result simply because English uses certain in that way.

`Cher` before a personal noun can express affection: `ma chère voisine`. After a thing noun it commonly means expensive: `un appareil cher`. The construction `cher à quelqu'un` means dear to someone and is not a price statement. `Cher` becomes `chère` in the feminine and `chers/chères` in the plural.
points: Vocabulary: `un résultat` (masculine), a result; `une voisine` (feminine), a female neighbour.
A particular reading before a noun is not the same as certainty about a proposition.

examples.french: Je cherche une **certaine** adresse près du canal.
examples.english: I am looking for a particular address near the canal.
examples.note: The speaker has one in mind but has not specified it.

examples.english: A definite improvement is already visible.
examples.note: The improvement is not in doubt.

examples.french: Ma **chère** voisine m'a prêté son vélo.
examples.english: My dear neighbour lent me her bicycle.
examples.note: `Cher` expresses affection before the personal noun.

examples.french: Cette réparation est trop **chère** pour moi.
examples.english: This repair is too expensive for me.

mistakes.why: `Cher` still agrees with the feminine noun `réparation`.

sections.title: Last in a series; real or true
paragraphs: With time units, `dernier` after the noun commonly identifies the preceding calendar period: `la semaine dernière`, last week. Before the noun it often marks the final member of a defined sequence: `la dernière semaine du stage`, the final week of the course. This is not a universal rule that every post-noun `dernier` means previous; learn the time expression and the intended sequence together.

`Vrai` before a noun often emphasizes genuine status or intensity: `un vrai problème`, a real problem. After a noun it commonly means factually true: `une histoire vraie`, a true story. Other combinations allow stylistic variation, and a `vraie histoire` can have more than one interpretation. Use clear contexts rather than claiming that position always creates a rigid opposite.
points: Vocabulary: `une semaine` (feminine), a week; `une histoire` (feminine), a story; `un problème` (masculine), a problem.
`Dernier` has `dernière, derniers, dernières`; `vrai` has `vraie, vrais, vraies`.

examples.french: Nous avons envoyé le dossier la semaine **dernière**.
examples.english: We sent the file last week.
examples.note: The week immediately before this one.

examples.french: La **dernière** semaine du stage sera consacrée au projet.
examples.english: The final week of the course will be devoted to the project.
examples.note: The final week within a specified course.

examples.french: L'absence de transport est un **vrai** problème.
examples.english: The lack of transport is a real problem.
examples.note: The speaker emphasizes its genuine importance.

examples.english: The film tells a true story.
examples.note: The events are presented as factually true.

sections.title: Situer dernier dans le temps
paragraphs: The contrast between `la semaine dernière` and `la dernière semaine` is useful, but it does not mean that every pre-noun `dernier` describes something final forever. `Le dernier bulletin` can mean the latest bulletin available now; a later one may still appear. `Ces derniers jours` and `ces dernières années` refer to a recent stretch continuing up to the present, not necessarily to the final days or years of something.

`La dernière fois` can refer either to a previous occasion or to an occasion intended to be final. Context supplies that distinction. Before a following clause, use `la dernière fois que`: do not mechanically move `dernière` after `fois` just because English means previous. `La fois dernière` is also possible as a standalone expression for a previous occasion, although `la dernière fois` is the more useful all-purpose pattern.
points: Vocabulary: `un bulletin` (masculine), a bulletin; `une fois` (feminine), an occasion.
Ask whether the reference is a preceding calendar period, the end of a specified series, the latest available item, or a previous occasion.

examples.french: **Ces derniers jours**, les températures ont baissé.
examples.english: Over the past few days, temperatures have fallen.
examples.note: A recent period, not the last days of a closed series.

examples.french: Voici **le dernier bulletin** ; le prochain paraîtra vendredi.
examples.english: Here is the latest bulletin; the next one will appear on Friday.

examples.french: **La dernière fois que** j'ai loué une voiture, j'ai choisi un petit modèle.
examples.english: The last time I rented a car, I chose a small model.
examples.note: A previous occasion; the clause follows the fixed pre-noun order.

practice.prompt: Using ancien, form the noun phrase my former employer. Use mon and employeur.
practice.explanation: Former status is normally expressed before the role noun.

practice.prompt: Using propre, form her own room with sa and chambre.
practice.explanation: Propre before the noun emphasizes ownership.

practice.prompt: Which phrase means a definite result, not a particular unspecified result?
Give last year using l'année and dernier for the preceding calendar year.
practice.explanation: Dernière follows the time unit for the preceding year.

practice.prompt: Form an antique wardrobe using une, armoire and ancien in the ordinary object-age position.
practice.explanation: Ancienne after the object describes its age.

practice.prompt: Form clean shoes using des, chaussures and propre.
practice.explanation: After the noun, propres describes cleanliness.

practice.prompt: Form a particular address using une, certain and adresse.
practice.explanation: Certain before the noun identifies an unspecified particular address.

practice.prompt: Form my dear friend for a woman using ma, cher and amie.
practice.explanation: The adjective separates ma from amie; chère expresses affection and agrees.

practice.prompt: Supply cher in the correct form: Ces machines sont trop ___.
Form the final day of the course using le, dernier, jour and du stage.
practice.explanation: Dernier precedes the noun for the final member of the sequence.

practice.prompt: Form a factually true story using une, histoire and vrai in the taught factual position.
practice.explanation: Vraie follows histoire in this factual contrast.

practice.prompt: Emphasize a genuine problem: use un, vrai and problème in the taught emphatic position.
practice.explanation: Vrai before the noun emphasizes that it is a real problem.

practice.prompt: Form our former neighbours using nos, ancien and voisins.
practice.explanation: Anciens is before the role noun and masculine plural.

practice.prompt: Form last month for the preceding month using le, mois and dernier.
practice.explanation: The ordinary preceding-calendar-period expression puts dernier after mois.

practice.prompt: Form their own ideas using leurs, propre and idées.
Choose the meaning of Ces souvenirs me sont chers.
choices: These memories are dear to me.
These memories cost me a lot of money.
answers: These memories are dear to me.
practice.explanation: Cher à someone expresses emotional value, not necessarily price.

practice.prompt: The archive says Le dernier rapport est disponible ; un autre sera publié en juin. What does dernier mean here?
choices: The most recent report so far.
The final report that will ever exist.
answers: The most recent report so far.
practice.explanation: The announced future report makes latest the intended reading. Position alone does not imply an end to publication.

practice.prompt: Supply dernier with agreement in the expression meaning over these past few years: Ces ___ années, le quartier a beaucoup changé.
practice.explanation: Ces dernières années describes a recent stretch; dernière agrees with feminine plural années.

practice.prompt: Put la, dernière and fois in the taught order before the clause. Supply only those three words: ___ que nous avons réservé, le site ne fonctionnait pas.
practice.explanation: La dernière fois que introduces a previous occasion followed by a clause. The calendar-period placement rule does not transfer mechanically to fois.

production_task.prompt: Describe a visit to a former workplace last week. Include `ancien` for a former role, `dernier` for the preceding week, `propre` for ownership, and either `cher` or `vrai` with a clear intended meaning.
production_task.model_answer: La semaine dernière, j'ai rendu visite à mon ancienne équipe. Mon ancienne responsable a maintenant son propre bureau. Elle m'a montré une armoire ancienne qu'elle a restaurée. Ces retrouvailles ont été un vrai plaisir.
production_task.translation: Last week, I visited my former team. My former manager now has her own office. She showed me an antique wardrobe that she restored. This reunion was a real pleasure.
rubric: Make former status distinct from the age of an object.
Use the correct time-unit placement for last week.
Keep adjective agreement as well as intended meaning.
